answer: The estimates are generally positive, but the evidence does not support a defensible conclusion that dark-skinned players have a higher sending-off probability. Across 181 estimates with confidence intervals, the median standardized effect was 0.0241, yet only 3 were statistically significant and positive, while 178 results were indeterminate and 64 universes were unavailable.
rationale: Positive point estimates are common, but statistical support is sparse and the multiverse has substantial indeterminacy and missingness. The evidence therefore cannot distinguish a supported positive effect from low-precision estimates that are compatible with no meaningful effect.
key_evidence: The median standardized estimate was 0.0241, with a first quartile of 0.0115 and third quartile of 0.0405.
Only 3 of 181 estimates with confidence intervals were statistically significant and positive; none were statistically significant and negative.
There were 178 indeterminate results and 64 unavailable universes among 245 universes; 735 of 768 expected results were reported.
Skin-tone combination medians ranged from 0.0225 to 0.0366, and threshold-specific medians ranged from 0.0211 to 0.0388.
refinement_reason: The broad claim depends on materially different skin-tone measurement and dichotomization rules, whose median estimates differ even though their signs do not reverse. These operationalizations should be specified rather than combined into one undifferentiated hypothesis.
suggested_hypotheses: Using the mean of both skin-tone raters and defining dark skin as a score above 0.5, dark-skinned players have a higher dyad-level probability of at least one sending-off than light-skinned players.
Using exact agreement between raters and defining dark skin as a score above 0.5, dark-skinned players have a higher dyad-level probability of at least one sending-off than light-skinned players.
Using a threshold of at least 0.75 for dark skin, dark-skinned players have a higher dyad-level probability of at least one sending-off than light-skinned players.
caveats: The supplied summary does not identify which specific multiverse specification was the prespecified primary analysis.
The standardized effect scale is not translated into an odds ratio or probability difference in the supplied evidence.
Non-significance does not establish that the effect is absent; the large number of indeterminate results indicates limited precision or unavailable inference.
The alternative model and exposure-handling choices also shift effect magnitudes, although their signs do not reverse.

sending_off_outcome.label: Sending-off outcome definition
sending_off_outcome.rationale: Which columns define the dyad-level indicator for at least one sending-off?  [found by: direct]

include_second_yellows.label: Include straight and second-yellow sendings-off
include_second_yellows.description: Set outcome = 1 when redCards > 0 or yellowReds > 0; otherwise set outcome = 0.

straight_red_only.label: Straight red cards only
straight_red_only.description: Set outcome = 1 when redCards > 0 and ignore yellowReds, even when yellowReds > 0.

skin_tone_combination.label: Combining the two skin-tone ratings
skin_tone_combination.rationale: How should rater1 and rater2 be combined into the player skin-tone score before dichotomization?  [found by: direct]

mean_raters.label: Mean of both raters
mean_raters.description: For every row, define skin_score = (rater1 + rater2) / 2.

rater1_only.label: Use rater 1 only
rater1_only.description: Define skin_score = rater1 for every row and ignore rater2.

rater2_only.label: Use rater 2 only
rater2_only.description: Define skin_score = rater2 for every row and ignore rater1.

conservative_agreement.label: Use only exact rater agreement
conservative_agreement.description: Retain rows only when rater1 = rater2, and define skin_score as that common value.

skin_tone_threshold.label: Binary skin-tone threshold
skin_tone_threshold.rationale: Which prespecified rule converts the combined skin-tone score into the dark-skinned exposure?  [found by: direct]

dark_at_least_half.label: Dark at score at least 0.5
dark_at_least_half.description: Define dark_skin = 1 when skin_score >= 0.5 and dark_skin = 0 otherwise; scores 0.5, 0.75, and 1 are dark.

dark_above_half.label: Dark above 0.5
dark_above_half.description: Define dark_skin = 1 when skin_score > 0.5 and dark_skin = 0 otherwise; only scores above 0.5 are dark.

dark_at_least_three_quarters.label: Dark at score at least 0.75
dark_at_least_three_quarters.description: Define dark_skin = 1 when skin_score >= 0.75 and dark_skin = 0 otherwise.

games_exposure_handling.label: Handling games as exposure
games_exposure_handling.rationale: How should the games column enter the dyad-level any-event logistic analysis?  [found by: direct]

unweighted_dyads.label: One equally weighted observation per dyad
unweighted_dyads.description: Fit the binary logistic model to the 146,028 dyad rows without weights; games is not used as a weight or offset.

games_frequency_weights.label: Weight dyads by games
games_frequency_weights.description: Fit the binary logistic model with games as a frequency weight, so a dyad with games = k contributes k times the likelihood contribution of a dyad with games = 1.

games_as_predictor.label: Adjust for games as a covariate
games_as_predictor.description: Fit the unweighted binary logistic model and include the numeric games column as a linear predictor; do not use it as a weight.

logistic_model_specification.label: Covariate and referee-effect specification
logistic_model_specification.rationale: Which predictor structure should be used for the dyad-level logistic model estimating the dark_skin odds ratio?  [found by: direct]

crude_logistic.label: Crude logistic model
crude_logistic.description: Fit outcome ~ dark_skin using a standard logistic link, with no additional columns and no referee effects.

adjusted_player_league_logistic.label: Adjust for league and player characteristics
adjusted_player_league_logistic.description: Fit outcome ~ dark_skin + leagueCountry + position + height + weight using a standard logistic link; do not include referee effects.

referee_fixed_effect_logistic.label: Add referee fixed effects
referee_fixed_effect_logistic.description: Fit outcome ~ dark_skin + leagueCountry + position + height + weight + factor(refNum) using a standard logistic link; omit any player fixed effect because dark_skin is constant within player.

crossed_random_intercepts.label: Crossed player and referee random intercepts
crossed_random_intercepts.description: Fit a logistic mixed model with fixed effect dark_skin and random intercepts (1 | playerShort) and (1 | refNum); include no other fixed covariates.

uncertainty_estimation.label: Uncertainty estimation for repeated dyads
uncertainty_estimation.rationale: How should standard errors and intervals for the dark_skin odds ratio account for repeated players and referees?  [found by: direct]

model_based_standard_errors.label: Model-based standard errors
model_based_standard_errors.description: Use the fitted logistic model's default model-based variance and report its Wald standard error and confidence interval.

two_way_cluster_robust.label: Two-way cluster-robust standard errors
two_way_cluster_robust.description: Estimate a sandwich variance clustered simultaneously by playerShort and refNum, and use it for the dark_skin odds ratio interval.

cluster_bootstrap.label: Cluster bootstrap
cluster_bootstrap.description: Resample playerShort clusters and refNum clusters using a two-way cluster bootstrap procedure, refit the selected model for each successful replicate, and use the bootstrap distribution for the interval.
